description: Jeu étiqueté du TD04 : 15 articles fictifs pour la RQ1 du sujet de référence. 'gold' = décision d'un comité de deux relecteurs humains. 'llm_demo' = réponse rejouée par le LLM de démonstration (objet JSON ou texte brut). 'cas' = ce que l'article rend observable.
question: Comment les LLM améliorent-ils le rappel du screening des SLR ?

papers.title: Large language models for title and abstract screening in software engineering SLRs
papers.abstract: We evaluate GPT-4 and two open LLMs as screeners for systematic literature reviews in software engineering. Across five published reviews, the LLM screening pipeline reached a recall of 0.96 while halving the manual workload.

reasons: LLM évalués pour le screening, rappel mesuré

evidence.quote: the LLM screening pipeline reached a recall of 0.96

papers.title: Generative AI as a second reviewer for study selection
papers.abstract: This paper studies generative AI assistants during study selection in software engineering reviews. The assistant flagged relevant primary studies with a sensitivity of 0.93 compared to two human reviewers.

reasons: IA générative pendant la sélection des études, sensibilité mesurée

evidence.quote: generative AI assistants during study selection

papers.cas: synonymes présents dans les termes du protocole

papers.title: LLM-based screening of randomized clinical trials for medical guidelines
papers.abstract: We apply large language models to the screening of clinical trial reports for medical guideline development. The models achieved a recall of 0.91 on 4,000 records about patients with diabetes.

reasons: domaine clinique : hors du périmètre génie logiciel

evidence.quote: screening of clinical trial reports for medical guideline development

papers.title: A blockchain framework for supply chain traceability
papers.abstract: We design a permissioned blockchain to trace goods across suppliers. A case study with three manufacturers shows reduced audit time.

reasons: sujet sans rapport avec le screening des revues

papers.title: Can LLMs reduce screening workload in mapping studies?
papers.abstract: We measure how much reading effort large language models save when screening candidate papers for software engineering mapping studies. The tool reduced the number of abstracts read by 60%, and only two relevant papers were missed.

reasons: LLM et screening ; le rappel est seulement suggéré (articles manqués)

evidence.quote: large language models save when screening candidate papers

papers.cas: critère implicite : le rappel est exprimé sans le mot

papers.title: LLM-assisted passenger screening at airport checkpoints
papers.abstract: We fine-tune a large language model to support security screening of passengers' declarations at airport checkpoints. The model detects suspicious declarations with a recall of 0.89.

reasons: screening de passagers : aucun lien avec les revues systématiques

papers.cas: piège lexical : tous les mots, mauvais sens

papers.title: Active learning to prioritise citation screening
papers.abstract: We compare three active learning strategies to prioritise records during citation screening in software engineering reviews. The best strategy reached 95% recall after reading 40% of the records.

evidence.quote: we use GPT-4 to rank the records

papers.title: Prompting LLMs for systematic review screening: a replication
Zero-shot LLM screening of primary studies
papers.abstract: We assess zero-shot prompting of an LLM for screening primary studies in three software engineering reviews and report recall and precision per review.
papers.llm_demo: This paper looks relevant to me, I would probably include it.

papers.title: Ensembles of LLMs for study selection in requirements engineering reviews
papers.abstract: We combine the votes of four LLMs during study selection for requirements engineering reviews. The ensemble improved recall by 8 points over the best single model.
papers.cas: LLM qui se trompe, peu confiant

papers.title: Editorial: generative AI and the future of evidence synthesis
papers.abstract: In this editorial, we discuss how generative AI may change screening and synthesis in systematic reviews, including risks for recall.

papers.title: GPT-4 as a screening assistant: false negatives in SE reviews
papers.abstract: We ask GPT-4 to screen titles and abstracts for six software engineering reviews and analyse its false negatives. The assistant missed 3% of the relevant studies while cutting reading time in half.

reasons: un LLM (GPT-4) trie titres et résumés ; les faux négatifs mesurent le rappel

evidence.quote: We ask GPT-4 to screen titles and abstracts

papers.cas: limite du lexique : aucun terme exact

papers.title: Benchmarking open LLMs for title and abstract screening
papers.abstract: We benchmark five open-weight LLMs on title and abstract screening for twelve software engineering SLRs. Recall ranged from 0.82 to 0.97 depending on the prompt.

reasons: comparaison de LLM pour le screening, rappel rapporté

evidence.quote: We benchmark five open-weight LLMs on title and abstract screening

papers.title: Sentiment analysis of developer chats with large language models
papers.abstract: We use large language models to classify the sentiment of 20,000 developer chat messages. The best model reached an F1 score of 0.81.

reasons: analyse de sentiments : pas de screening de revue

papers.title: Triage of candidate studies with GPT-4 in software engineering tertiary studies
papers.abstract: We let GPT-4 triage candidate papers for two tertiary studies in software engineering. Only 2 of 310 relevant papers were missed, and reviewers accepted most of its suggestions.

reasons: le résumé ne mentionne ni screening ni rappel

papers.cas: les deux évaluateurs d'accord… et tous deux dans l'erreur
